findings.text: `reflect.TypeOf(arg).String()` panics with a nil-pointer dereference when an argument is an untyped nil, because `reflect.TypeOf(nil)` returns a nil `reflect.Type`. The old `fmt.Sprintf("%s", ...)` handled that case and printed `%!s(<nil>)`. For example, `Arguments{nil}.String()` now panics. This is reachable through mock failure messages and diffs, for example when a mocked method is called with a nil argument.
